out.rationale: Chen et al. ask for notions of equilibrium better suited to language games. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that a profile is a valid interactive proof system iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of nip, while noting worst-case losses and Stackelberg equilibria are hard to learn; Chen et al. instead use Nash equilibria of zero-sum games.

out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols in their single-message game. Hammond and Adam-Day prove that for problems with a valid proof system a profile is a valid interactive proof iff it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of nip, which has alternating messages and worst-case losses.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: correspondence between verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria and valid proof protocols, extended to multi-turn interaction

text: Theorem 8 states that for a probabilistic decision problem that has a valid proof system, a strategy profile is a valid interactive proof system if and only if it is an approximate verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium of the nip game. The authors note this leaves two difficulties: learning to minimise the worst-case rather than expected loss, and finding a Stackelberg equilibrium.
title: Theorem 8: valid interactive proofs = verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of nip
